A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same feedback-linearization research. All 30 pages of each version, including figures, equations, references, and appendices, support comparison despite substantial reformatting and some mathematical inconsistencies.

before.justification: v2 reports original numerical simulations for heterogeneous logistic regression and IEEE-39/IEEE-118 optimal power flow in Figures 2–3.

after.justification: v3 reports logistic-regression and power-flow simulations, additional PDGD/ALM comparisons, and a quadratic-programming experiment comparing approximate FL controllers in Figures 2–5.

M1.justification: Appendix B.2 adds approximate FL using an approximate inverse F(x), and approximate FL-PI incorporating integral feedback of constraint violations. This introduces a substantive controller extension; the existing FL-proximal, FL-Newton, and momentum procedures are retained.

E1.justification: v3 adds a synthetic quadratic-programming test with Gaussian-generated coefficients and stated affine inequality constraints. Heterogeneous logistic regression and both IEEE power-flow cases remain; moving power flow to Appendix B.3 does not remove coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Appendix B.1, Figure 3 adds evaluated PDGD and ALM comparators to logistic regression, substantially extending v2's comparison among FL variants. The power-flow legend's change from FL to FL-proximal denotes the retained method, not another baseline.

E3.justification: The new approximation experiment specifies 20 variables, 10 constraints, and trajectories through 5,000 iterations. Logistic-regression Figure 2 now displays 300 rather than 200 iterations, while five clients and 200 samples per client remain specified. Changes to initialization or numerical step sizes are not documented.

E4.justification: Appendix B.2 introduces a robustness analysis of inverse-approximation error, comparing approximate FL with and without integral feedback. This tests whether the PI component remedies failure under approximate inversion, a question not experimentally investigated in v2.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, uncertainty intervals, error bars, or significance tests for its simulations. The added figures continue the same convergence-curve reporting practice.

E6.justification: Figure 2 replaces the logistic-regression objective and KKT trajectories; matching initialization and other settings are insufficiently documented to infer a same-setting performance improvement. New Figure 3 reports PDGD/ALM performance comparable to FL-proximal, and Figure 4 reports approximate FL stagnation versus a roughly 10^-12 KKT gap for FL-PI. Power-flow findings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix C.1 adds Assumption 7 and Theorem 6, asserting exponential objective-gap convergence for strongly convex objectives with affine equality constraints. Formal hypotheses also change: the inequality controller requires a finite rather than unique solution, Theorem 2 explicitly requires LICQ, and Theorem 5 omits the separately numbered LICQ assumption previously included among its hypotheses.

C1.justification: The abstract removes the explicit assertion that the momentum algorithm achieves faster convergence. Introduction contribution 4 now distinguishes empirical acceleration from the proved O(1/sqrt(T)) guarantee for nonconvex equality constraints. The four central contributions otherwise remain.

C2.justification: New remarks explain computational cost in terms of constraint count, argue for PI robustness under approximate inversion, and position FL against other first-order approaches. New qualifications distinguish KKT convergence from reaching local/global optima or avoiding saddles. Existing LICQ restrictions, unproved momentum acceleration, and the IEEE-118 ill-conditioning hypothesis are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix B.2 documents a reciprocal-diagonal inverse approximation and the dimensions and Gaussian construction of its quadratic test problem. These provide limited new implementation information, but numerical controller gains, step sizes, and code access are still not supplied.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands positioning against close alternatives, adding control-barrier and nonsmooth constrained-optimization work, including Allibhoy–Cortés and Muehlebach–Jordan. It acknowledges prior momentum methods under nonlinear constraints, distinguishes their dynamics and discretizations, and argues that FL permits a broader choice of constraint controllers.

P1.justification: v3 selectively rewrites introductory and contribution passages, adds titled remarks, separates assumptions, and changes some Lyapunov-function terminology to merit function. Power flow moves into a new numerical appendix and subsequent appendices are reorganized, while the main section sequence and much existing prose remain.

P2.justification: The document adopts NeurIPS formatting with a redesigned author block, different typography, denser equation layouts, and resized figures. Figure 1 becomes wrapped by text; Figure 2 changes plotted scales and trajectories; two figures are added; and the power-flow figure moves to the appendix with standardized legend names.

improvement.justification: External-baseline comparisons, the PI robustness study, and clearer qualifications provide useful additions. However, new Theorem 6 claims a gain-independent exponential rate while its proof drops K and does not justify the bound for general infeasible starts. Appendix B.2 also pairs an equality-form controller with a stated inequality problem. These unresolved issues in the new scientific material prevent a reliable judgment that the benefits outweigh the validity concerns.
